svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop
svg.desc: Interactive botanical learning sheet: drop the ten word-bank labels (petal, sepal, stamen, pistil, anther, filament, ovary, style, stigma, receptacle) onto a labelled longitudinal diagram of a dicot flower, with hint, answer-check and reset popups.

g.text: Drag & Drop Lab • Angiosperm (flowering plant) morphology
click a word-bank tile, then click the empty slot it highlights
BLOOM DIAGRAM — NOT TO SCALE • stamens shown as a ring of 10 around the pistil
Pick a label from the word bank below.
Click the highlighted empty slot on the diagram.
Use CHECK ANSWER to review your work.
Hover a word to preview its target slot.
Everything is stored inside the SVG file.
the link between the flower and the next generation
pick a label, then click its empty slot on the diagram
10 labels • click a tile to drop it on the diagram
Most students confuse the STAMEN (male) with the PISTIL (female).
The pistil is the single structure in the very centre of the flower:
• STIGMA — the sticky tip on top (it catches pollen grains)
• STYLE — the slender stalk below the stigma
• OVARY — the swollen base that holds the ovules
The STAMEN is made of an ANTHER (the yellow tip) sitting on a
FILAMENT (the thin stalk). Look for the yellow ovals that ring
the centre of the flower — that is the stamen ring.
The PETALS are the big pink blades. The SEPALS are the narrow
green blades hiding behind them. The RECEPTACLE is the green
platform at the very base where every part is attached.
Green leaf that protected the bud
Sticky tip that receives the pollen
Platform where all floral parts attach
ALL TEN PARTS PLACED — EXCELLENT WORK
Every label in the word bank has been dropped into its slot.
